design.rationale: Accuracy deductions come from internal contradictions, not from false platform claims: superseded ARC/UI positions remain normative in four sections (F-04); a schema admits an executor backend that the forwarding rules make impossible (F-02); the callback_descriptors CHECK forces false materialization claims (F-03); 'pinned plan' versus 'rejected with stale_contract' (F-08); container/deployment labels misstate the APK's interactions and the CallbackFlow view is consistent with a forbidden protocol reading (F-01, F-12, F-13); the same class carries disjoint contracts across code views and the design-doc class table uses a different vocabulary (F-11); two reason-code grammars (F-14); 'or'-joined delete semantics and a credential-kind rule that contradicts its own separation claim (F-15); an ARC identifier of unverified provenance presented as what existing clients use (F-18). Completeness deductions: no model path for tools/call dispatch, resources/subscribe/read, cancel and cleanup (F-01); concrete-class callbacks unclassified (F-03); subscription transition table for death/lease/timeout absent (F-07); health tuple and AppBar status element never specified once (F-09); paired-ADB ownership, client realization and deployment topology (F-10); pairing message sequence and TLS host candidate (F-06); negotiated direct stream is a placeholder (F-17); envelope 1.0 vs package 0.8.0 absent from inspected text (F-18); storyboards cover three of the required flow families with placeholder panels (F-19); canonicalization unpinned for cross-language hashes (F-16); toolchain pins incomplete for the determinism claim (F-20). Credits: every requirement has a specified mechanism in prose except the direct stream; protected-owner authentication, pairing proof, Binder acquisition routes, backpressure, startup reuse, lease renewal, admin-route gating, brightness range, MCP resource/journal semantics and ARC framing facts were verified consistent across independent slices and the pinned proto. Scores are not averaged across workpapers; each is a single judgment of the whole design.
